commits.message:
refactor(style)!: styled text reaches the wire only through segmentsToString

Style.render(text, colorSystem?) was a second ANSI encoder beside
segmentsToString: it could not express a null colour depth, always emitted
OSC 8 links whatever the destination took, and nested SGR inside the link
where the serializer nests the link inside SGR. Nothing in src/ called it.
segmentToString(new Segment(text, style), destination) is the one encoder,
and the style byte tests now go through it with the same assertions.

BREAKING CHANGE: Style.render is removed; use
segmentToString(new Segment(text, style), destination).

refactor(render)!: the serializer takes where it writes as one Destination

segmentsToString(segments, destination) and segmentToString(segment,
destination) replace the positional colorSystem + hyperlinks pair, so a call
reads segmentsToString(segs, resolveDestination("auto")) or
{ colorSystem: ColorDepth.TRUECOLOR, hyperlinks: true } instead of a bare
`true`, and a depth can no longer be paired with a link setting taken from a
different destination.

Console, Live, Screen and renderToString hand their destination through
whole. renderToString applies its overrides (noColor, hyperlinks) once, where
it builds the value; Console applies its hyperlinks override once, in its
constructor. Console.destination replaces Console.hyperlinks, so Live reads
the value its console encodes for rather than two of its fields.

BREAKING CHANGE: segmentsToString and segmentToString take a Destination
in place of (colorSystem, hyperlinks). Console.hyperlinks is removed; read
console.destination.hyperlinks.

feat(strip)!: the default powerline lead is a notch cut into the first cell (#160)

* feat(strip)!: the default powerline lead is a notch cut into the first cell

POWERLINE_JOINER_GLYPHS leads with U+E0D6 (inverse right-arrow) instead of
U+E0B2. Drawn by the existing cap painter (fg = the cell's background, no bg),
it inks the top-left and bottom-left of the cell and leaves a right-pointing
triangle empty, so a coloured run opens notched, as if an arrow before it
pointed in. The notch is the terminal's own background showing through, so it
matches under a translucent terminal background; a reverse-video U+E0B0 notch
drew visibly darker there. The arrow, divider and tail are unchanged.

BREAKING CHANGE: new PowerlineJoiner() draws U+E0D6 as its lead cap, not U+E0B2.
Pass { ...POWERLINE_JOINER_GLYPHS, lead: "" } for the old shape.

* chore(release)!: 0.17.0

The default powerline lead changed shape, which is breaking for 0.x.

* fix(strip): the notch lead is U+E0D7, not U+E0D6

U+E0D6 is Nerd Fonts ple-right_hard_divider_inverse: beside a coloured cell it
draws a left-pointing hole, an arrow pointing out of the run. The notch the
ticket describes, and the name it cites (ple-left_hard_divider_inverse), is
U+E0D7: an empty triangle based on the cell's left edge, pointing into the run.
Outlines read from JetBrainsMonoNerdFont-Regular.ttf with fontTools.

docs/strip.md and the POWERLINE_JOINER_GLYPHS comment describe the shape
correctly and say the lead is a Powerline Extra glyph that classic
powerline-patched fonts lack; the join() table no longer describes the lead
as reaching back.

* test(strip): the default-lead comment reads as sentences
